scenarios.scenario: wrong process on the port (another program listens on 3000)
scenarios.rationale: The script stops whatever listens on the web port by PID, by design (that is the incident fix). The dry run names PID and process name first; PC-7/PC-11 replay it with a decoy. A listener owned by another user or a protected PID fails closed with exit 5 rather than being skipped.

scenarios.scenario: system PID (4 or less) owns the port
scenarios.rationale: Stop-WebPortListener refuses ids of 4 or less and logs "is protected; refusing to stop it", exit 5. Shape test covers the guard text; not run on the PC.

scenarios.scenario: self PID (this script owns the port)
scenarios.rationale: The listener id equal to $PID is refused with exit 5. Shape test only.

scenarios.scenario: port reused by another user's process
scenarios.rationale: Stop-Process may be denied; the script re-checks with Get-Process, logs "could not stop PID <id>: <message>." and exits 5. Not exercised on the PC (single-user machine).
After the stop the script waits at most 10 s and then logs "still in use after 10s; not continuing." and exits 5; nothing is started over a live listener. Shape test only.

scenarios.scenario: port listing fails silently (reads as port free)
scenarios.rationale: A thrown failure of Get-NetTCPConnection is fail closed (exit 5). A silent empty result would read as free and the new bind then fails; the smoke check then reports a failure and exit 6, or the old server still answers with the old build id and the smoke check compares it to the marker. W1 user report: no throw on a free port at 314bc0a.

build-web.ps1 removes the marker before the build and writes it only after pnpm exits 0; the stale check also compares BUILD_ID to the marker build_id. Shape tests; W2 PC run saw build ids change with a fresh marker.

The marker is written only when the build exit code is 0; a failed build leaves no marker, so start-web.ps1 refuses with exit 4 ("no build marker"). Shape test; the refusal text for a missing marker is not yet pasted from the PC.
start-web.ps1 refuses with "Stale build: no build marker. Run deploy\build-web.ps1, then start again.", exit 4; README documents the first-start rebuild. Not pasted from the PC (PC-6).

scenarios.scenario: restart loop between an old script instance and a new one
scenarios.rationale: A second start stops the first (observed on the PC at 08:56: the hand-started instance logged "Web process exited with code 1"). The README warns against a hand start while the task runs. A task retry storm is bounded by Task Scheduler retries; not proven beyond the observed case.

scenarios.scenario: smoke false positive from a stale process
scenarios.rationale: The check needs HTTP 200 and the served build id (marker file, else HTML) equal to the marker build_id, and stops early when the child exits; an old server with an old build id would not match. Its limit: the port was freed first, so a stale process there is already gone. HTTP non-200 and mismatch branches were never exercised on the PC (known gap).

The URL is built from the script's own Tailscale address and the web port only; the NET-scan gate checks no literal remote host in deploy. A system proxy would be honoured by Invoke-WebRequest (not the case on the home PC).

scenarios.scenario: secrets in the marker or logs
scenarios.rationale: The marker holds schema, commit, web tree, dirty flag, build id and times only; logs hold ports, PIDs and process names. S-secret-scan and PS-secret-scan gates on added lines print nothing.
